OpenAPI 3.1.0, Kairos 0.18.1.

Every endpoint is served under the tenant resolved from the request host and requires a bearer token; see [Configuration](../configuration/) for how a deployment resolves both. The live spec is at `/api/openapi.json`.

A write can be complete when its answer does not get to the client (a timeout, an upgrade). Some routes take an optional `Idempotency-Key` header, and each of these routes lists it. The key has 8 to 128 characters: letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `:` and `-`. A UUID is a good key.

Send a new key with each new request, and the same key when you retry it. The key belongs to the person and the agent key. A second request with the same key in 24 hours writes nothing. Its answer has the status and the body of the first answer, and the header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

The server refuses the same key with a different route, path or body with 409 `REQUEST_KEY_REUSED`. A refused request keeps no key, so its retry runs again. The MCP `request_key` uses the same keys (KAIROS-A-0065).

This page is generated from that spec, so it cannot drift from the router — but it describes only *what exists*. For how to do something, see the how-to guides; for why the API is shaped this way, see the explanation pages.

## Contents

- [Work items](../rest/work-items/) — The five entity families. Every one has the same shape — list, get, create, update, delete — and the same optimistic-concurrency contract on update (KAIROS-A-0004): submit the `version` you read, and a concurrent edit gets 409 with the current entity in `details.current`. A write to a claimed task by a different person gets the header `Kairos-Warning: <code> claimed by <name> since <time>` (KAIROS-T-0359). A task with open blockers can move into a claims column or a done column. That answer gets the header `Kairos-Warning: <code> moved into <column>, blocked by <blocker> (open)` (KAIROS-T-0565).
- [Across any work item](../rest/across-any-work-item/) — Operations addressed by `{entity_type}` and a short code, so they work uniformly across the five families.
- [Boards and teams](../rest/boards-and-teams/) — Board configuration, membership, the team structures that own boards, and the grants of `manage_structure` (KAIROS-T-0337).
- [Execution scope](../rest/execution-scope/) — Repositories as first-class execution scope (KAIROS-A-0019) and the git forges behind them.
- [Tenant configuration](../rest/tenant-configuration/) — Org-admin surfaces: the metadata and template definitions that shape what work items can carry.
- [Machine access](../rest/machine-access/) — Agent keys of a person, service accounts and their API keys, and the SCIM tokens for directory sync.
- [The deployment itself](../rest/the-deployment-itself/) — Activity, administration, and what the deployment reports about itself.
- [Signing in](../rest/signing-in/) — Sessions, and local password accounts (KAIROS-I-0018). `/api/login` and `/api/local-accounts` are only on a deployment with `KAIROS_LOCAL_AUTH` on. `/api/session` and `/api/logout` are on each deployment (KAIROS-T-0364). `/api/login` and `/api/logout` are unauthenticated by nature. Everything under `/api/local-accounts` is org-admin only, including the reads: a list of somebody's live sessions is a security surface rather than work content.
- [Schemas](../rest/schemas/) — the wire shapes that the operations above reference.
